class: A success judged from loose wording on a page that is not a confirmation
symptom: The dashboard showed the application as submitted ("Already submitted on site -- confirmed by portal") while it was still on the create-account page; a false submitted record also makes the agent refuse to apply for that job again.
root_cause: The confirmation pattern accepted "thank you for your interest", which opens employers' create-account and job pages ("Thank you for your interest in a career with HonorHealth. Please create an account ..."). The text alone was taken as proof, and nothing checked that the page had stopped asking for anything.
why_tests_missed: The confirmation tests used real confirmation pages; none used a page that thanks the candidate and still shows a form.
fix: CONFIRMATION_TEXT keeps only a confirmation's own words ("thank you for applying", "we have received your application", "you've already applied"); _site_confirms also requires that neither the page nor any frame shows a password box or three or more boxes to fill in. The false record was corrected by hand.
prevention: Record a terminal state such as 'submitted' only from positive evidence that cannot appear earlier in the flow (a confirmation's own words, a portal listing, an email), and check the page has stopped asking for input. Never let politeness or a generic phrase decide it.
